1_Learning_Objective.Title: 🎯 The "Why Are We Learning This?" (Learning Objective)
1_Learning_Objective.Content: The core takeaway is to help your child understand that everything around them has a name. They will learn to categorize words into four groups: People, Places, Animals, and Things. This builds their descriptive vocabulary!

2_The_Hook.Title: 🪝 The Hook (How to start the conversation)
2_The_Hook.Content: Look around the room, point to an object, and ask: **'Imagine if nothing in the world had a name. If you wanted an apple, you'd have to say, "Please give me that red, round, crunchy thing!"'** (Laugh together at how silly that sounds). **'Names make life so much easier! Let's find out what naming words are.'**

Mini_Lessons.What_To_Say: Tell your child: 'Everyone we know has a name. Boy, girl, teacher, doctor, and even Mom and Dad are naming words for people!'
Mini_Lessons.Home_Example: Look at family photos and point out different people. Say, 'Grandpa is a naming word for a person!'

Mini_Lessons.What_To_Say: Tell your child: 'Everywhere we go has a name too. The park, the school, the kitchen, and the zoo are all naming words for places.'
Mini_Lessons.Home_Example: Ask them, 'Where do we go to buy groceries?' When they answer 'The store,' tell them, 'Yes! Store is a naming word for a place.'

Mini_Lessons.Topic: Lesson 3: Names of Animals and Things
Mini_Lessons.What_To_Say: Tell your child: 'All your toys, clothes, and favorite animals have names. Dog, cat, ball, and book are all naming words.'
Mini_Lessons.Home_Example: Pick up a toy car. Ask, 'Is this a person? No. Is it a place? No. It's a thing! Car is a naming word for a thing.'

4_Common_Stumbling_Blocks.Title: 🚧 Common Stumbling Blocks (What to watch out for)
4_Common_Stumbling_Blocks.Content:
Kids often confuse action words (like 'running' or 'jumping') with naming words. 
*   **How to clarify:** Ask the 'Touch Test' question: 'Can you touch or see a "jump" sitting on the table? No! But can you touch a "shoe"? Yes! So shoe is a naming word.'

Questions.Question: Is 'Dog' a naming word for a person or an animal?
Can you tell me a naming word for a place where you go to play on the swings?
If I say 'The baby is crying', which word is the naming word for the person?

Activities.Name: 1. Sticky Note Labels
Activities.Description: Give your child a stack of sticky notes (you can write the words or draw pictures). Have them run around the house and stick them on 'Things' (door, bed, table).

Activities.Name: 2. Naming Word I-Spy
Activities.Description: Play a game of I-Spy but use categories: 'I spy with my little eye, a naming word for a Thing that is blue...'

Activities.Name: 3. The Sorting Hat
Activities.Description: Draw a grid with four boxes: Person, Place, Animal, Thing. Call out random words (e.g., 'Monkey', 'School', 'Sister') and have them point to the right box.
